U.S. BANK PAYMENT CARD
QUICK-REFERENCE GUIDE
Welcome to U.S. Bank Healthcare Payment Solutions, the spending account program that helps you make smart benefit
decisions and take control of your costs - and your care. This quick-reference guide will help you get started, from activating
your card and exploring your new benefits... to using your account everyday.
If you have any questions or want more information, help is only a click or call away. Simply contact U.S. Bank Consumer
Services at 877-470-1771 (M-F 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. CT), or visit www.mycdh.usbank.com.
When can I begin using my new payment card?
First, activate your card (the number is on your activation sticker) and your account online. If you have an HSA, you
can begin using your account when funds are available. Contributions can be made through payroll deductions, online, by
making a contribution to your account, or by mailing a personal check and the HSA Contribution Form
(available online). If you have an FSA or HRA, you can begin using your account as soon as it has been activated and funds
are deposited and available.
Where can I use my card?
You can use your card at hospitals and doctor's offices, as well as drugstores, pharmacies, and grocery stores that have
either an IIAS (Inventory Information Approval System) (IIAS) or certified that 90% of their gross sales are eligible. To
find a list of merchants, log in to your account, select the favorite merchant accepts your card, visit the "Useful Links & Resources" section or
go to www.usbank.com.
What if I need to pay for purchases?
You can pay for purchases with your payment card at the point of sale. If you need card information on your provider's billing statement, use
the card number on your card. If you need a reimbursement check, use the reimbursement request form associated with your card - simply select
the "Reimbursement" tab online and sign any required forms.
What expenses are eligible?
Your account can be used for medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug expenses.
Generally, items are considered eligible if it relates to the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or preven-
tion of disease, or for the purpose of affecting any structure or function of the body, including qualified long-term care expenses and
certain over-the-counter drugs, transportation to receive care, etc. For a complete list of qualified expenses, see IRS Publication 502 available on
the IRS website.
What if a purchase is for items that are not qualified?
If you purchase over-the-counter (OTC) drugs that have been prescribed by your doctor.
Am I required to pay back if it's an eligible expense?
If a merchant is IIAS-certified, the card will determine if the purchase is eligible. If your provider does not accept your card by
IIAS, you may need to submit a claim for reimbursement or you may need to either split the transaction or use an alternate form
of payment.
How do I check my balance?
You can check your balance online, by phone, or at the point of sale. More than a few
ways are available to check your balance.
What happens if I have an overage?
If you have an overage in your spending account or for something you paid for with your card, how does the system know?
If you use your card and there are no funds in your spending account or if the purchase is for more than the account
balance, the transaction will be denied. You can check your balance online or on-site and we take care of the rest.
What if I need to pay for a purchase and don't have my card?
If you pay out-of-pocket for an eligible expense, you can request a reimbursement. However, fee-some FSA purchases, the validation may be
required. You may need to provide any receipts or statements for at least six-months beyond the end of your plan year.
Will I still need to submit documentation?
For HSAs, so please check the website for your plan's specific rules on documentation.
You will receive an email if documentation is required. For any purchase, where you do send my documentation.
If substantiation is required, please log in to our website. Or, you can send the substantiation form found on the website via
You can scan and upload your documentation, or HCB CS, P.O. Box 6122, Fargo, ND 58108-6122. You can
also e-mail mysubstantiation@usbank.com or fax 888-403-5029.
Can I reimburse myself with funds for qualified medical expenses incurred before I enrolled in an HSA?
No. Qualified medical expenses may be reimbursed tax free only if the expenses are incurred after the date your HSA is
established.
What should I do if my card is ever lost or stolen?
